seen.where: https://www.zobodat.at/pdf/MGSL_125_0395-0399.pdf (read in Chrome 29 Oct 2026, Anubis proof-of-work passed automatically): K.-H. Ludwig, 'Geheimschrift im Bauernkrieg', Mitt. Ges. Salzburger Landeskunde 125 (1985), pp. 395-399; letter held at Salzburger Landesarchiv (SLA), Geh. Arch. XVI/1
seen.extent: One letter of Archbishop Matthaeus Lang, Salzburg, 19 May 1526 (Pfingstsamstag), about 15 lines, ciphered in the passage from 'Wir ... Zwayer vandl' onwards, printed in facsimile-style transcription on p. 397
seen.cipher: Monoalphabetic substitution with Latin-letter/figure/sign symbols, one symbol per letter with a few doubles (e: 2 and 8; f/v, u/w, b/p, i/j/y merged); Ludwig broke it by hand and prints the full 'Salzburger Code von 1526' table and a verbatim plain-text transcription on p. 399 (read also independently by Hofrat Herbert Klein after WWII).

prior_art.decode: Not searched on DECODE's own site (login wall); known.py for Burkhard von Ems / Matthaeus Lang / Salzburger Landesarchiv found only the lead itself and an unrelated 1513-14 Lang item already marked read; not a DECODE-held record as far as the repo dumps show.
prior_art.tomokiyo: No cryptiana page on this letter found by web search (Salzburg 1526 Geheimschrift searches 29 Oct 2026).
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry paper or GL.htm entry on it found by web search.
prior_art.edition: The letter is printed in Ludwig 1985 itself: cipher transcription p. 397 and the deciphered text p. 399; his footnote 4 only says the letter belongs to the context of Vogt's 1883 edition of the Artzt correspondence (ZHVSN 10, p. 168), not that Vogt printed it.
prior_art.literature: Ludwig 1985 (read in full, 5 pp.); the lead's description 'discussed as undeciphered' was a misreading of the web summary, the article opens with the failed computer attempt and then solves the letter.

vetting.key_check: No outside key needed: Ludwig reconstructs the key from the letter itself (frequency analysis plus the 'sch/ch' crib) and publishes it; checked it is a complete a-z table, so nothing further to apply.
vetting.duplicates: known.py searched 'Burkhard von Ems', 'Matthaeus Lang', 'Salzburger Landesarchiv', 'Bauernkrieg': no other record of this letter in leads, catalogue or targets (Ehingen 1525 is a different Swabian file).
vetting.closed: Deciphered and the key and plain text printed by Ludwig, MGSL 125 (1985) pp. 395-399; nothing left to decipher.

seen.extent: Six letters, Rome, 6 Aug 1548 to Dec 1550, 12 leaves; only the first letter (3 images) was opened. Its first leaf carries 9 full lines of cipher figures, the other letters are described by the BNE as 'seis cartas parcialmente cifradas'.
seen.cipher: Italian letter (6 Aug 1548) in clear with a block of continuous digit strings (no separators, one- and two-digit values, about 9 lines) after 'con tutto il core'; between the cipher lines there is no interlinear decipherment and nothing written in the margins of that leaf (the clear marginal notes are summary headings of the letter). Letters 2-6 not individually opened.
